place_fields.summary: Chunchi Falls is a stepped waterfall on the Arkavathi River near Mullahalli/Harroshivanahalli in the Kanakapura area of Ramanagara district, set among rocky granite terrain.
place_fields.best_time: August to February, especially after the monsoon

planning_attributes.description: A rocky, stepped cascade on the Arkavathi River; published descriptions place the falls en route to Sangama and Mekedatu and note a downhill walk over uneven rocks to the falls.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The name is associated with local folklore about Chuncha and Chunchi.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Approach from Kanakapura toward Sangama; published route descriptions identify a turn toward Chunchi Falls near the Harroshivanahalli/Yelegabalu side and a final walk to the falls.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Google Maps currently lists the attraction as temporarily closed.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The approach includes uneven/rocky terrain and a downhill walk; sources warn about slippery rocks, deep gorge areas and strong currents.
planning_attributes.notes: The falls are on the Arkavathi River and are commonly visited with Sangama and Mekedatu.

place_fields.summary: Ramanagara falls is a tourist attraction listed in Voddarahalli, Karnataka, about 5.24 km from Ramanagaram railway station.

planning_attributes.description: A tourist attraction identified in public place listings as Ramanagara falls in Voddarahalli, Karnataka.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Public listings place it in Voddarahalli, with Ramanagaram railway station about 5.24 km away.
planning_attributes.notes: The available place listing describes it as a tourist attraction and reports visitor reviews mentioning weekend visits.

place_fields.micro_region: Basavana Betta Forest, Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary
place_fields.summary: Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary is a protected area spanning parts of Mandya, Chamarajanagar and Ramanagara districts, with the Cauvery River running through dry deciduous and riverine forests.

planning_attributes.description: A large protected wildlife landscape known for riverine habitats, dry deciduous forests, wildlife and nature-based activities including trekking and rafting.
planning_attributes.elevation_or_height: The sanctuary spans roughly 125 to 1,514 metres in elevation.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Established as Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary in 1987 under the Wildlife Protection Act framework; the protected area was later expanded.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Karnataka Tourism identifies Kanakapura as a nearby town and notes road access via NH 209; the sanctuary covers a large multi-district area rather than a single gate.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Safaris and stays require booking; angling is permit-based according to Karnataka Tourism.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: This is a wildlife sanctuary with elephants, leopards and marsh crocodiles; visitors should follow forest-department access and safety rules.
planning_attributes.local_name_variants: Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary; Kaveri Wildlife Sanctuary
planning_attributes.notes: Basavanabetta/ Basavana Betta is one of the reserve forests included in the sanctuary; the supplied point is in the Mandya-Ramanagara zone.
